newsitem.title: GERMANY: German oilseed crushers find Santer plan premature.
newsitem.headline: German oilseed crushers find Santer plan premature.

text.p: German oilseed processor grouping Verband Deutscher Oelmuehlen (VDO) believes a new draft plan on farm area aid reform by the European Union Commission is too hasty, an official said in response to an enquiry.
"The plan seeks to decouple aid payments from specific crops which is a step in the right direction," she said.
But the sector needs more time to adjust to changes.
"Otherwise, production could plummet and newly-built crushing capacity may have to be closed with all the typical macro-economic consequences that would bring."
VDO represents 22 companies which together last year processed 7.3 million tonnes of oilseeds out of a 28 million tonne EU total.
Oilseed producer organisation UFOP said earlier the draft plan, which is due to be issued on Wednesday, could threaten oilseeds production at the expense of grains.
It would raise cereals aid by 12 Ecus a tonne while reducing present oilseeds aid by over a third.
The VDO official said crushers supported decoupling, which the EU Commission was pushing in order to comply with demands likely to be made in future world trade rounds.

But they feared while this political goal was desirable, radical reform of the EU area aid system could cause market chaos, not just in the EU, by generating price-based, alternating production cycles of grains and oilseeds.

The spokeswoman said VDO members expected current oilseeds production patterns could be maintained until the end of the next WTO round, which could be in the year 2003. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
